item.title: Go Daily Question 20250603
item.description:
What is the output of the following code? Why?

func main() {

    var m = [...]int{1, 2, 3}

    for i, v := range m {
        go func() {
            fmt.Println(i, v)
        }()
    }

    time.Sleep(time.Second * 3)
}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

Before Go 1.22: 2 3 2 3 2 3 The for range loop uses short variable declaration (:=) to iterate variables. It’s important to note that variables i and v are reused in each loop iteration, not re-declared.

item.title: Go Daily Question 20250602
item.description:
Will the following code terminate normally?

func main() {
    v := []int{1, 2, 3}
    for i := range v {
        v = append(v, i)
    }
}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

It will not result in an infinite loop and will terminate normally.

The number of iterations is determined before the loop starts. Changing the length of the slice within the loop does not affect the number of iterations.

item.title: Go Daily Question 104
item.description:
Is the output of the following code correct?

        {"A"},
        {"B"},
        {"C"},
    }
    s2 := make([]*Foo, len(s1))
    for i, value := range s1 {
        s2[i] = &value
    }
    fmt.Println(s1[0], s1[1], s1[2])
    fmt.Println(s2[0], s2[1], s2[2])
}
Output:
{A} {B} {C}
&{A} &{B} &{C}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

After Go 1.22, the output is normal. Before Go 1.22: The for range loop reuses the value variable. The address of value is the same throughout, so the output for s2 would become CCC.

item.title: Go Daily Question 103
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

func main() {
    var a = []int{1, 2, 3, 4, 5}
    var r [5]int

    for i, v := range a {
        if i == 0 {
            a[1] = 12
            a[2] = 13
        }
        r[i] = v
    }
    fmt.Println("r = ", r)
    fmt.Println("a = ", a)
}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

r = [1 12 13 4 5] a = [1 12 13 4 5] range a actually operates on a copy of variable a. Due to the structure of slices, these two slices will point to the same underlying array. Therefore, changes to a[1] = 12 and a[2] = 13 will affect the structure of v.
